**Reading (mechanism, round-6 root-cause, round-7/8/9 corrected probe)**: the f_target overhead grows linearly with tensor bytes (~9–14 GB/s signature, fixed ~15 µs at 2^10). Event capture attributes it: the fix routes complex `zero_` to `x.copy_(0)` and complex `zeros` to `empty` + that same path; **native ATen complex-scalar copy itself stages the value through a full-tensor pageable HtoD** — profiler memcpy ≈ 570 µs at 2^20 c64 under registration, and the same overhead appears NATIVE without flag_gems (`copy_(0)` 0.82–0.83 ms vs native `zero_()` 0.004–0.006 ms device memset). PRE-BUILT device-scalar copy-only net cost, by probe batch (timing variation between runs, not a functional difference; batch/device/protocol provenance in the logs): **round-7 batch 0.0071/0.0069 ms, round-8 batch 0.0089/0.0067 ms** (c64/c128; archives `zero-staging-attribution-r7-batch.log` and `zero-staging-attribution.log`). The earlier ~0.02 ms figure mixed in per-call `.cuda()` construction and is superseded; device-scalar creation is 0.336 ms single-shot (含冷启动/first-launch overhead) / 0.015 ms 50-iter average, one-off outside any steady-state copy; see `zero-staging-attribution*.log`, `zeros-hitprobe-*.json`). So the dominant cost is the inherited ATen complex-scalar copy path, not extra FlagGems compute; it is a candidate performance follow-up (FIX-ITEM-3, three candidate paths + correctness matrix), with no optimization number promised.

- **registered** (asserted per family, f_target fails hard if missing): see `registered_target_keys` in each JSON.
- **probe-hit** (torch.profiler CUDA events, full lists in `zeros-hitprobe-{f_target,native}.json`): under f_target, `zeros` shows a NATIVE at::native FillFunctor + pageable HtoD memcpy, `zero_` shows ONLY the pageable HtoD memcpy; **no Triton kernel name appears for the zeros family**. Triton kernel names (e.g. `sum_dim_kernel_inner`, `_absolute_complex_kernel`) ARE observed for the a-sum-abs family, and conv2d/linear kernels for b-linear. Kernel-name recognition: at::native elementwise kernels are classified native; triton kernels appear as their own function names (convention), raw names kept verbatim.
